pull.title: script: clarify implicit signature-cache input requirements
pull.body:
**Problem:** Signature-cache hashing relies on input requirements that are implicit at its public entry methods.
Inspired by the Elements rangeproof-cache vulnerability behind the recent [Liquid incident](https://blog.blockstream.com/liquid-network-security-incident-assessment) and the [subsequent cache-key fix](https://github.com/ElementsProject/elements/pull/1600), this change clarifies an easy-to-misread hashing pattern: `Write(data, size)` hashes the data bytes without encoding the size.
Bitcoin Core's cache keys already include the signature hash, public key, and signature in separate ECDSA and Schnorr domains.
Bitcoin Core's signature-cache encoding is unambiguous for inputs accepted by its current script checker: a valid ECDSA public key's prefix determines its length, while a Schnorr public key is always 32 bytes, leaving the signature as the remaining suffix.

**Fix:** Use native `HashWriter` serialization in the typed `ComputeEntry*` methods so ECDSA public keys and signature vectors include their CompactSize lengths.
Schnorr retains its fixed-size public-key encoding and raw signature span.
Return the digest by value from the public `ComputeEntry*` methods so callers explicitly initialize the cache entry, where the previous chained `Finalize(entry.begin())` obscured the output assignment.
Keep the prepared salt prefixes private and const, and copy them locally for each entry.
Retain the ECDSA salt padding and drop the Schnorr salt padding.
Add a nonce-taking constructor so tests can reproduce the encoding deterministically.
The process-local cache-entry bytes change, while script validity rules are unchanged.

concept ACK on the tests, concept NACKy on the refactors due to blast radius. Will review the tests closer if split out

I ran the two script_tests.json rows this adds or changes, at c8d6a97afb366f82680601713942afb4955c2885, through btclib's script interpreter, and both give the expected result. I haven't reviewed the sigcache changes.

> concept NACKy on the refactors due to blast radius

The refactor is the meat of this change, the original error would still be possible even if we only add tests, and I want to make sure we learn from those mistakes and refactor to make such misunderstandings harder.
If we're afraid of touching a part of the code, it means it's not ours yet, and it's probably where the ugly bugs are buried.

Concept ACK

The new tests catch five signature-cache bugs that the current unit tests miss. I made seven one-line breaking changes to `sigcache.cpp` and ran the unit tests on c8d6a97afb36 and on its base, d4b0e1e4b0.

On the base, the unit tests still pass with six of the seven changes. Only storing failed Schnorr checks is caught, by `txvalidationcache_tests`. On this PR, `script_tests` catches five of those six: dropping the public key or the sighash from the ECDSA or the Schnorr entry, and storing failed ECDSA checks. The cached passes in `DoTest` catch the ECDSA ones, and the new BIP341 vector checks catch the Schnorr ones.

The sixth change gives Schnorr entries the ECDSA salt, and no unit test catches it on either commit. The separate salts are all that keeps the two domains apart: with one salt, the ECDSA entry for a 33-byte key and a 63-byte signature equals the Schnorr entry for the key's first 32 bytes and a signature made of the key's last byte followed by those 63 bytes. A test that builds both entries with `ComputeEntryECDSA` and `ComputeEntrySchnorr` and checks that they differ passes on this PR and fails with that change. It could go in this PR; I can share it, and the seven changes.

Rebased and replaced the hashing helper and cache-entry assertions with native serialization (with explicit size commitment), following the [Liquid fix](https://github.com/ElementsProject/elements/pull/1600) and @instagibbs's suggestion.
Made the salt prefixes const, removed the padding, and added tests that check the encoded bytes and make sure failed signature checks aren't cached.

script: prepare immutable signature-cache prefixes

Make both prepared hash prefixes const `HashWriter` members and copy them inside `ComputeEntryECDSA` and `ComputeEntrySchnorr` before hashing an entry.
Serialize the nonce followed by a one-byte signature-type tag.
Keep 31 zero bytes after the ECDSA tag so the first SHA256 block is compressed once during construction.
With it, 70-72-byte ECDSA signatures need three compressions per entry for both compressed and uncompressed keys, while unpadded uncompressed keys would need four.
Drop the Schnorr padding, since Schnorr still needs three compressions and was slightly faster in local ARM SHA256 measurements.
The cache is process-local, so the changed entry bytes have no persisted compatibility effect.
Add a nonce-taking constructor so encoding tests do not depend on global RNG sequencing.
Characterize the raw field encoding in these public methods before the following native-serialization change.

Suggested by Yudis-bit: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36395#discussion_r4499982215

Co-authored-by: Yudis-bit <Yudis-bit@proton.me>

comments.body:
The padding in master was there to fill a 64-byte chunk so the compression ran once at startup. With 33 bytes, the constructor leaves 33 bytes in the buffer and defers that transform into `ComputeEntry`.

For 65-byte uncompressed keys this also crosses the 192-byte mark, needing 4 transforms instead of 3.

Padding 31 zero bytes keeps the `HashWriter` changes and the precomputed chunk:

```cpp
HashWriter{} << nonce << uint8_t{'E'} << std::array<uint8_t, 31>{}
```

Indeed, while Schnorr measured slightly faster without it (must be some alignment magic), there is an extra cost for uncompressed ECDSA keys: I restored the padding for ECDSA and added you as coauthor, thanks.
